prompt:
I need the front end for Codeshelf Municipal. The building and zoning code reference used by a mid-sized city's permitting department, where staff and members of the public read the adopted codes, local amendments and interpretation memos.

Who's using it: Priya Natarajan, technical publications coordinator in the city's Development Services department. She owns how the reference behaves for the department's 46 plan reviewers and inspectors and for the public.

What they're doing right now: City council has adopted the 2024 building code with 31 local amendments, effective January 1, 2027. Projects submitted before that date are still reviewed under the 2021 edition. Priya is changing the reference's settings so the right edition opens by default for each audience. Plan reviewers should get the edition that matches a permit's application date. Field inspectors should get an offline bundle that includes both editions on their tablets. The public site should show 2024 with plain-language summaries and a notice about the transition. She is also choosing which superseded interpretation memos get retired or kept with a 'historical' label. Before publishing, she needs to see what each audience will get.

What's in the system at this point: Code editions held: 2018 (archived), 2021 with 24 local amendments (current), 2024 with 31 local amendments (adopted Oct 21, 2026, effective Jan 1, 2027). Interpretation memos: 87 total, of which 19 reference 2021 sections that changed in 2024, and 6 are flagged by the building official for retirement. Audiences: plan reviewers (22 staff), field inspectors (24 staff on tablets, current offline bundle 1.8 GB, last synced Nov 3), counter staff (9) and the public (about 4,200 visits a month). Current defaults: everyone sees 2021, amendments are shown inline, plain-language summaries are on for the public only, and the reading-level target is grade 8. Supported languages: English and Spanish, with Vietnamese summaries in progress (40% done). Settings changes need a second approver: Deputy Building Official Marcus Bell.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
